Crisis level remains 4 (High); base 15%, stress 45%, tail 40%.

todaysEvents.delta: Reuters reported Oct 1, citing Marisks, that three Liberian-flagged oil tankers were hit by unknown projectiles during Sep 29 Hormuz transits with AIS switched off.
Reuters reported Sep 30 that Iran received a US response through Qatari mediators. An official said the parties disagree on sequencing; no signed reopening agreement was reported.
Reuters Oct 1, citing four sources, reports Chinese refiners halted oil-product exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau. December Brent settled at $102.31 (+4.37%); Yahoo BZ=F is a separate observation.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Qatari mediation produces agreed sequencing and a monitored reopening. A US response has been received, but a signed agreement and durable shipping normalisation remain unverified.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: Selective Qatar-linked LNG passages and recovered oil exports coexist with tanker attacks and restricted Hormuz access. Current replacement supply, freight and cargo cost observations remain incomplete.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Sequencing disagreements persist or attacks further disrupt Hormuz and alternative export routes. Marisks reported three tankers struck on Sep 29; insurance and replacement LNG costs remain unverified.

e-reuters-oil-0925.title: Oil slides as US-Iran truce hopes outweigh Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
e-reuters-oil-0925.note: Reuters reported Brent settled at 104.32 USD/bbl on Sep 25, down 2.1%, as truce hopes outweighed attack risk. The article also reported Brent at 105.11 at 05:41 GMT, six Houthi missiles intercepted near Taif/Yanbu, and no resumption of Yanbu tanker loadings.

e-reuters-saudi-sts-0925.title: Gulf of Oman ship-to-ship oil transfers reach limit as Saudi exports surge
e-reuters-saudi-sts-0925.note: Reuters reported September Saudi crude exports via Hormuz on track for 3.6 million bpd, while Gulf of Oman ship-to-ship operations reached capacity. A $1.27 million/day Middle East-to-China VLCC time-charter quote was reported for Sep 21.

e-hormuz-talks.title: Iran-Gulf talks shelved as Oman says conditions not right
e-hormuz-talks.note: Re-scraped The National's Sep 14 article. It records Oman's postponement of the proposed Iran-Gulf meeting; its traffic figures remain dated historical context.

e-hormuz-route-policy-0927.title: Strait of Hormuz tensions linger as Iran and US move further from a deal
e-hormuz-route-policy-0927.note: Al Jazeera reported Sep 27 that Tehran instructed shipping companies to use a temporary Iran-approved Hormuz route and pay fees; full reopening remains conditional on ending the US blockade. Reports of explosions were attributed to Iranian media and were not confirmed by Iranian authorities.

e-hormuz-total-transits.note: Al Jazeera reported Kpler data showing Hormuz daily vessel transits ranging from 5 to 11 this week against a 10-day average of about 13, still well below pre-crisis norms.

e-ap-hormuz-20260818.title: US, Iran engaged in tanker war: Where is the months-long conflict headed?
e-ap-hormuz-20260818.note: Al Jazeera reported the US and Iran fought a direct tanker war Sep 5-6: CENTCOM struck three Iranian oil tankers while Iran fired missiles at a US carrier and destroyer and hit three tankers plus three US-linked vessels.

e-saudi-pipeline.title: Oil settles up around 4% as Iran's president vows to never surrender
e-saudi-pipeline.note: Reuters reported Sep 23 that Saudi Arabia restarted its East-West pipeline to the Red Sea, while indirect US-Iran talks discussed reopening Hormuz and lifting the US naval blockade. Iran's position on reopening remained conditional.

e-hormuz-single-digit-crossings.title: US-Iran conflict helps drive wave of supertanker orders
e-hormuz-single-digit-crossings.note: Reuters reported Sep 17 that Strait of Hormuz tanker crossings remain in single digits (LSEG data) as shipowners order a record wave of VLCCs to serve longer Atlantic-to-Asia routes.

e-nakilat-charters.title: QatarEnergy and Nakilat sign long-term charter agreements for 25 LNG vessels
e-nakilat-charters.note: Verified current official Nakilat release: 25 conventional LNG vessels, each 174,000 cubic metres, owned by Nakilat and chartered to QatarEnergy affiliates.

e-reuters-policy-0929.title: Qatari mediators press peace deal between US and Iran
e-reuters-policy-0929.note: Qatar said it was exchanging messages between the US and Iran to establish common ground. Trump denied offering sanctions relief or release of frozen funds; negotiations had not produced a Hormuz reopening agreement.

e-reuters-oil-0929.title: Oil prices settle down 2.5% on signs Middle East exports recovering
e-reuters-oil-0929.note: Reuters reported Saudi Arabia resumed Yanbu tanker loadings after restarting East-West Pipeline operations. Reuters reported Sep 29 Brent settlement at $102.59/bbl and WTI at $89.38/bbl; these are separate settlement observations from Yahoo snapshots.

e-reuters-attacks-1001.title: Three oil tankers hit by projectiles in Hormuz strait on Tuesday, Marisks says
e-reuters-attacks-1001.note: Marisks reported three Liberian-flagged oil tankers were struck by unknown projectiles while transiting Hormuz on Sep 29. Reuters names Al Ruwais, Mersin Prosperity and Sinbad; Marisks said AIS transponders were off.

e-reuters-talks-0930.title: Iran says it receives US response to latest proposal
e-reuters-talks-0930.note: Iran said it received a US response to its latest proposal. An official briefed on the talks said the parties disagree about the sequence of steps; no reopening agreement was reported.

e-reuters-lng-0928.title: Qatar-linked LNG traffic through Hormuz strait picks up despite conflict
e-reuters-lng-0928.note: Reuters/LSEG/Kpler tracked GasLog Skagen off Sri Lanka Sep 27 with a Ras Laffan cargo. Al Shamal reappeared outside Hormuz around Sep 24-25; Al Ghashamiya delivered to Dahej Sep 24. The report describes individual sightings and dark AIS transits, not a complete comparable weekly LNG count.

e-reuters-oil-1001.title: Oil jumps 4% on reports China halts fuel exports, US troops head to Middle East
e-reuters-oil-1001.note: Reuters reports Chinese refiners suspended oil-product exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau, citing four sources. The new front-month December Brent contract settled at $102.31, +4.37%; WTI settled at $92.87, +2.71%, on Oct 1. Reuters cites a Wall Street Journal report that the US is sending a third aircraft carrier and up to 10,000 additional troops; these deployments are reported plans.
